title: Dedicated capacity: certification for real-workload throughput and autoscaler validation
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build and execute a repeatable certification process for Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees that validates autoscaling policies and fleet controls using replayed customer traces and synthetic signature workloads. Deliver a test harness, methodology doc, and customer-facing acceptance checklist so sales/solutions can sign off capacity commitments.
background: Customers expect provisioned Dedicated pools to meet contractual throughput with predictable latency and autoscaling behavior. Existing synthetic prober runs don't capture tail-latency and multi-tenant interference seen in production traces. We need a validated certification workflow that combines real workload replay, policy-driven autoscaler tests, and controlled degradation injections to prove SLOs and provide deterministic acceptance criteria.
objectives: Create a load harness that replays anonymized customer traces and can synthesize signature-shaped traffic
Define a benchmarking methodology that measures throughput per GPU, end-to-end latency percentiles, and autoscaler responsiveness
Produce a customer acceptance checklist and runbook for Dedicated on-boarding
Expose instrumentation and dashboards for deterministic pass/fail and cost accounting
out_of_scope: Full multi-region failover certification (this ticket covers single-region fleet and autoscaler behavior). On-prem private appliance integration deferred to later cycle.
approach: We will build a modular harness: (1) trace ingestion and signature extraction, (2) workload synthesizer capable of concurrency shaping and token-distribution control, (3) policy-driven autoscaler tester that supports ramp, spike, and gradual-traffic-shift scenarios, and (4) chaos injector for simulating node failures and network degradation. Test runs include baseline (no interference), multi-tenant interference matrix, autoscaler policy validation, and customer-acceptance replay with golden traces.
measurement_methodology: Primary metrics: sustained token/sec per GPU, requests/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end), error-rate, autoscaler scale-up latency, and cache hit ratio
Sampling windows: 10s windows for autoscaler events; 60s windows for sustained throughput calculation; 30m steady-state for acceptance runs
Aggregation: report both fleet-level and node-level percentiles. Include run-to-run variance and delta against baseline
Cost accounting: record estimated GPU-hours per certified throughput point and attach to acceptance report
test_plan: TT-1: Implement trace replay adapter and signature extractor (supporting JSONL traces and protobuf call events)
TT-2: Implement workload synthesizer with concurrency shaping and per-client KV-cache affinity toggles
TT-3: Create autoscaler policy templates (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and mapped acceptance scenarios
TT-4: Build chaos injector to drop 5-20% of nodes and emulate network latency for tail-latency analysis
TT-5: Run baseline and interference matrix, collect metrics, and iterate parameter tuning
TT-6: Run customer acceptance replay for two anonymized customer traces and produce final report and checklist
steps: 1) Gather 3 anonymized customer traces from Data Platform and sanitize PII (Priya to coordinate)
2) Extract workload signatures and create synthetic variants (short-chat-heavy, long-context-heavy, embedding-burst)
3) Deploy harness into dedicated-load-lab and connect to dedicated fleet staging cluster
4) Execute baseline run: target 70% of provisioned throughput for 30 minutes to establish baseline metrics
5) Execute autoscaler scenarios: ramp (10%->100% over 5m), spike (instant 4x for 2m), and step-downs to verify scale-down hysteresis
6) Run interference matrix: overlay synthetic tenants with 10/30/50% background load and measure tail-latency growth
7) Run chaos tests: kill 1/3 of nodes sequentially and measure request loss, failover latency, and autoscaler reaction
8) Produce acceptance report and sign-off checklist for Solutions and Customer Success
success_criteria: S1: For each certified throughput point, p95 end-to-end latency < 250ms and p99 < 500ms under specified concurrency
S2: Error rate <= 0.1% sustained across a 30m steady-state window
S3: Autoscaler scale-up completes within configured target (default template: < 90s from threshold breach to capacity available)
S4: Under multi-tenant interference (30% background synthetic neighbors), throughput degradation <= 15% vs baseline
S5: Run reproducibility: two independent runs within 10% throughput variance and < 5% change in p99 latency
S6: All customer-acceptance runs produce a checklist with explicit pass/fail and a signed artifact for Solutions-Engineering handoff
run_history: 2026-01-20: initial proof-of-concept harness run. Findings: concurrency shaping works, KV cache affinity not yet plumbed (Priya).
2026-02-02: baseline run at 50% provisioned capacity. Observed p99 spikes ~700ms during cache warmup. Action: add warmup phase to harness.
2026-02-10: autoscaler template 'balanced' trial. Observed scale-up latency ~120s due to scheduling queue. Action: tune pre-warm hooks and decrease cooldown.
2026-02-22: interference matrix run with two synthetic tenants at 30% load. Throughput drop observed ~12%, within expected. Need to document mitigation guidance for customer sizing.
risks: Anonymized traces may still contain sensitive metadata—data platform coordination required
Autoscaler behavior in staging may differ from production scheduling/backfills
Chaos injections could destabilize shared infra if mis-targeted
Reproducibility risk due to background noisy neighbors on the lab cluster
mitigation: Enforce strict trace sanitization and approvals before ingestion
Run critical certification runs on a reserved isolation pool to eliminate noisy neighbors
Add a pre-check safety gate in the chaos injector that verifies target node list
Capture full environment snapshots (versions, kernel, runtime, model build ids) with each run for reproducibility
